UnitStatement: proposal-format briefs require ScopePath as the run/context anchor, normally the deliverable folder.
proposal-format briefs require TaskSkill to be proposal-format.
proposal-format briefs require RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH as an absolute path to the deliverable folder.
When Tasks is omitted, proposal-format runs a baseline assessment.
ApplyEdits defaults to false and controls whether proposed changes are applied.
UseSemanticLensing defaults to false and controls whether Lens tags are included.
RuntimeOverrides.MaxProposals defaults to 10 as a soft cap on proposals.
RuntimeOverrides.FocusDocs defaults to all documents and restricts assessment to named docs when provided.
RuntimeOverrides.ProposalDepth defaults to full and accepts summary or full.
RuntimeOverrides.IncludeLensTags defaults to false and enables Lens tags without full lensing.
Every PROPOSAL block must contain Evidence, Change, Why, Risk, and Status.
Evidence must cite a file and section or heading, or location TBD.
Change descriptions must be actionable without further interpretation.
Status values are PROPOSED by default, APPLIED only when an edit was made, and NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING for contradictions or trade-offs.
No proposal may lack supporting evidence.
The decision interface must include MISSING, NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING, and DEPENDENCY_NOTES sections, even when they are none.
All proposals must reference content within the single deliverable scope.
If no production documents exist, proposal-format reports that in MISSING.
If no meaningful issues are found, proposal-format states that explicitly instead of padding output.
If specified Tasks cannot be completed, proposal-format reports them in MISSING with the reason.
Baseline scans must assess at least one category among completeness, consistency, verification, source fidelity, and identity.
Baseline scans report TBD items separately from proposals.
Baseline scans report dependency notes when cross-deliverable interfaces are visible.
proposal-format produces structured, evidence-grounded recommendations for deliverable-local work using the PROPOSAL block format.
proposal-format standardizes findings so they are reviewable, actionable, and traceable.
The PROPOSAL pattern is the canonical recommendation format for deliverable-local tasks.
The PROPOSAL pattern separates evidence from judgment, makes risk explicit, and preserves human authority over acceptance.
proposal-format is suitable for the TASK generic shell with no profile.
proposal-format requires ScopePath as an input.
proposal-format requires RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH as an input.
Tasks optionally specify concrete asks; when omitted, proposal-format produces a baseline scan.
RuntimeOverrides.MaxProposals optionally sets the soft cap on generated proposals.
RuntimeOverrides.FocusDocs optionally restricts analysis to named production documents.
RuntimeOverrides.IncludeLensTags optionally adds Lens tags when semantic lensing is not active.
ProposalDepth controls whether output is summary or full, defaulting to full.
proposal-format requires no deterministic tools.
When combined with deterministic-tool skills, proposal-format uses the other tool output as its evidence base.
proposal-format must not invent evidence to justify a proposal.
proposal-format must not widen scope beyond the single deliverable.
proposal-format must not edit outside the bounded task brief's write authorization.
proposal-format must surface contradictions in NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING instead of resolving them silently.
Every recommendation must be expressed as a PROPOSAL block.
A PROPOSAL block contains a short title, Evidence, Change, Why, Risk, and Status fields.
When semantic lensing is active or IncludeLensTags is true, a PROPOSAL block may include a Lens field.
The Lens field may be UNKNOWN when _SEMANTIC.md is missing.
Evidence must cite a file and best-effort section or heading.
Evidence must not cite _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md because it is a worklist, not authority.
Change must be precise enough to apply without further interpretation.
Why must name the improvement category rather than restating the change.
Risk must name concrete downstream effects.
PROPOSED is the default Status when the human has not decided.
APPLIED status is used only when ApplyEdits is true and the edit was made.
NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING status is used for genuine trade-offs, contradictions, or scope decisions.
Proposals may be grouped by issue type when practical.
Practical proposal groups include completeness gaps, consistency issues, verification gaps, source fidelity issues, and identity or terminology issues.
After proposal blocks, proposal-format always includes MISSING, NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING, and DEPENDENCY_NOTES.
Decision-interface sections may each be none when empty.
When Tasks is omitted from the brief, proposal-format produces a baseline assessment.
A baseline assessment returns top proposals up to MaxProposals, top TBD items, and top dependency notes.
Baseline scan is the default behavior, not a separate mode.
proposal-format outputs PROPOSAL blocks, MISSING items, NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING items, and DEPENDENCY_NOTES items.
Applied edits are optional and only occur when ApplyEdits is true.
MEMORY.md updates are optional and only occur when explicitly authorized by the brief.
Every proposal must cite evidence from production documents or accessible sources.
Unknowns remain TBD; proposal-format must not invent content to fill gaps.
Conflicts must be surfaced in NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING rather than reconciled silently.
Proposed changes must be minimal and reversible.
The human decides acceptance; proposals are recommendations, not directives.
proposal-format is reasoning-first; no deterministic tool ordering applies.
proposal-format has no TASK-enforced deterministic allowlist.
proposal-format declares no operational helper tools.
All proposal-format phases are performed by direct LLM reasoning against deliverable-local content under RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH.
proposal-format disallows hidden reliance on tools outside the declared list unless the human expands AllowedTools.
proposal-format writes are limited to the effective bounded task brief's write authorization for the single deliverable.
Optional applied edits require ApplyEdits true, and MEMORY.md updates require explicit brief authorization.
